about: Explain Back sketch grading fixtures (docs/features/explain-back-sketch.md). Sketches are block.sketch vector data in the card's pixels (350 x 240). expect is the visible grade's VERDICT. The unit tests read these without a model; tests/evals/explain-back-sketch.mjs grades them for real, by hand only.
prompt: In your own words: what happens between token id `2` entering nanoGPT and the model producing next-token scores?
expects: the id selects a row of the embedding table
transformer blocks mix the vectors across positions
the LM head turns the final vector into one score per vocabulary token

fixtures.why: A labelled pipeline that demonstrates every key idea, with no typed text: it must earn concept credit.

shapes.text: transformer blocks mix the vectors across positions
LM head: one score per vocabulary token

fixtures.why: A drawing that shows none of the key ideas: having a drawing earns nothing.
A labelled sketch whose mechanism is wrong (the id is used as a number): wrong marks earn no credit.
The text covers the first two ideas and the sketch the last two: only judged as ONE response does it cover all four.
fixtures.answer: Token id 2 picks row 2 of the embedding table, and a position embedding is added to that vector.

shapes.text: transformer blocks mix the vectors across positions
LM head: a score for every vocabulary token

fixtures.why: The same text without the sketch misses two ideas, so the complementary case is good only because of the sketch.
fixtures.answer: Token id 2 picks row 2 of the embedding table, and a position embedding is added to that vector.
